findings.title: Alert page restored from the back/forward cache keeps an unsaved status choice and a stale shown_status, so a later assignee-only save still overwrites another analyst's status
findings.repro: Full Chromium with bfcache on (channel 'chromium', ignoreDefaultArgs ['--disable-back-forward-cache']), fixed-AHM-03: with mg_actor=Ahmad open /alerts/<telnet id> (status New), choose Investigating in the Status list but do not save, click Upload, from another client PATCH /api/alerts/<id> {status:'resolved'} as Fiona, press Back (the page comes back from bfcache: pageshow persisted=true), type an assignee, Save.
findings.evidence: scripts/c6_status.js bfcache run (logs/c6-bfcache.log): 'afterBack': {select:'investigating', shown_status:'new', autocomplete:'off', persisted:true} -> stored 'investigating/"Ahmad"', audit [['Ahmad',{assignee:{from:'',to:'Ahmad'},status:{from:'resolved',to:'investigating'}}]]. With bfcache off (Playwright default) the same flow keeps 'resolved' (select 'new' after Back, audit assignee only), which is the form-restore case the fix targets. The original fails both ways. The frozen page is the person's own unsaved choice, so this is an edit conflict rather than a browser artifact, but the page gives no sign that the status changed meanwhile.
findings.fix: On the alert page, reload the status form when the page is shown again from bfcache (window.addEventListener('pageshow', e => { if (e.persisted) htmx.ajax('GET', location.pathname, {select:'#status-form', target:'#status-form', swap:'outerHTML'}) })), or have PATCH /alerts/{id}/status refuse a status change when shown_status no longer matches the stored status and answer the form with 'Someone changed this alert to Resolved meanwhile; check and save again.'

Add one IPv6 alert (scripts/add_ipv6.py) and open / at 1280 px: three pills broken (shots/fixed-06-v6-queue-1280.png); the original at the same widths shows 'Medium' on one line (shots/orig-all-v6-queue-1280.png). Script: node scripts/s5e_sweep.js fixed-06 (and orig-all).
findings.evidence: Sweep, shipped CSS, common data: 'common analyst default shipped ... mid-word: 701:unencrypted/Medium/Unencrypted 720:Medium 768:Medium 800:Medium 834:Medium 900:Medium 1024:Medium'; with DejaVu Sans '701:unencrypted/01:31:42/01:31:25/Medium/certificate/01:38:21/Unencrypted/01:34:53 ...'; home mode DejaVu '701:passwords/encryption./01:31:42/everything/passwords,/01:31:25/Medium:/certificate./01:38:21/encrypted./01:34:53'. Original (orig-all) at the same widths: 'mid-word: 320:172.18.0.2:4437' only (a mono cell on a phone, same in both). Timeline 768 px: 'Kind -> conn' broken only on fixed-06. Cause: per CSS Text 3, 'anywhere' counts every character as a break opportunity for min-content sizing, so an over-full auto-layout table (an IPv6 pair or long titles) shrinks every column below its words; 'break-word' does not. Candidate matrix (scripts/s5c_matrix.js, s5d_v6.js, s5e_sweep.js, s5f_assignee.js): putting white-space: nowrap back on .sev (V6) brings back the Home-mode sideways scroll the earlier reviewer removed it for ('common home default V6 sideways: 701->752 720->752'); plain break-word on every cell (V1) widens the page to 2031 px with a long name; word-break: break-word (V3) behaves exactly like anywhere in Chromium; V7 (below) has no mid-word break at any width/font/mode, keeps the 100-char name from widening the page ('one 100-char name V7 sideways: none'), and its only sideways case, 701 px with DejaVu Sans (-> 720), is identical to the original build.
findings.fix:
Verified in agentwork/r3-review/verify (57 tests pass, sweep clean), full diff at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-maxguard/d28fe4b6-2c9f-5cd0-8e7f-d2be65aa4c01/scratchpad/agentwork/r3-review/proposed-fixes.diff. maxguard/web/static/app.css:
-.banner, .status-form, .stack td { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
+/* Not "anywhere" on every table cell: the table layout then squeezes a column down to one
+   character and breaks short words ("Mediu/m"). A cell breaks between words; only the mono
+   addresses and the free-text Assignee may break inside one. Phones: see the media rule. */
+.banner, .status-form { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
+.stack td { overflow-wrap: break-word; }
+.stack td.mono, .stack td[data-label="Assignee"] { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
 and inside @media (max-width: 700px), after the .stack td grid rule:
+  .stack td { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }  /* a block now, not a column: nothing to squeeze */
 tests/unit/test_web.py: replace the CSS string assertion with
+    assert ".banner, .status-form { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }" in css
+    assert ".stack td { overflow-wrap: break-word; }" in css
+    assert '.stack td.mono, .stack td[data-label="Assignee"] { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }' in css

findings.title: text_field() stringifies non-text parts: an 'assignee' sent as a file part stores the first 100 characters of repr(UploadFile) (its multipart headers) as the assignee; control characters such as NUL are stored too
findings.repro: python scripts/s7_hostile_form.py fixed-06, case 4: PATCH /alerts/{id}/status with files={'assignee': ('x.txt', b'Mallory', 'text/plain')}; case 7: assignee 'Ann\x00Lee'.
findings.evidence: case 4 -> 200 'Saved.'; stored assignee='UploadFile(filename=\'x.txt\', size=7, headers=Headers({\'content-disposition\': \'form-data; name="assig' (audited the same way); case 7 -> stored 'Ann\x00Lee'. The original build does the same ('ORIGINAL build, assignee as file part -> 200 \'UploadFile(filename=...'). Only a hostile client can do this and it could store any 100-character text anyway, so the impact is garbage in the audit trail, not a security issue. With the fix: case 4 stores assignee=''.
findings.fix:
maxguard/web/routes.py (in the verified diff):
 def text_field(value) -> str:
+    if not isinstance(value, str):
+        return ""
-    return str(value).replace("\r", "").replace("\n", "").strip()
+    return value.replace("\r", "").replace("\n", "").strip()
plus the test added to test_status_change_is_saved_and_audited (file part -> assignee ''). Whether other control characters should be dropped as valid_name does for the actor is a policy choice (it would also drop ZWNJ/ideographic spaces from real names), so it is only noted here.

verdicts.reason: [Finding: alert page restored from bfcache keeps an unsaved status choice] Reproduced exactly on a fresh fixed-AHM-03 build with bfcache on (channel 'chromium', ignoreDefaultArgs ['--disable-back-forward-cache'], Chromium 141.0.7390.37): afterBack {select:'investigating', shown_status:'new', autocomplete:'off', persisted:true} -> stored 'investigating/"Ahmad"', audit [['Ahmad',{assignee:{from:'',to:'Ahmad'},status:{from:'resolved',to:'investigating'}}]]; with the Playwright default (bfcache off) the same flow keeps 'resolved' (select 'new' after Back, audit assignee only). But my variants (scripts/f1_variants.js, bfcache on, fixed-03) show this is not a Back/bfcache defect of the change: b2, the person never touches the Status list before leaving, Back from bfcache (persisted:true), types an assignee, Save -> stored 'resolved/"Ahmad"', audit {assignee:{from:'',to:'Ahmad'}} only, i.e. the true assignee-only save the change targets is correct under bfcache; b3, no navigation at all (choose Investigating, Fiona resolves meanwhile, type assignee, Save) -> the same 'investigating/"Ahmad"' overwrite with status resolved->investigating; b4, Reload after Back then Save -> 'resolved/"Ahmad"'. The original build gives the identical result in the finding's flow (orig-03 bfcache: stored investigating/"Ahmad"). So the submitted form is not an 'assignee-only save': the Status list shows the value the person chose themselves, and the fixed rule 'save only what this person changed on the form they saw' behaves as designed. What remains is a last-writer-wins conflict on a field both people edited, which happens without any Back (b3) and which this change never claimed to solve; a conflict check or a pageshow refresh of the form would be a new feature (reasonable follow-up), not a defect of this change. Unchanged problem outside the change's scope.

[Finding: overflow-wrap: anywhere on .stack td squeezes columns, 'Mediu/m'] Reproduced on a fresh fixed-AHM-06 build (web files byte-identical to fix3/ref), shipped CSS, default font, Analyst mode, after uploading telnet, ftp, plain_http and cert_self_signed (scripts/f1b_pills.js): 'fixed-06 ipv4 analyst 768  pills=High:1line,High:1line,Medium:2lines,Medium:2lines sevCol=83px table=736px scroll=768 broken=["Severity:Medium"]', the same at 701 and 1024 px; 1280 clean. After add_ipv6.py (one IPv6 alert): 'fixed-06 ipv6 analyst 1280 pills=High:1line,High:1line,Medium:2lines,Medium:2lines,Medium:2lines sevCol=85px table=1168px scroll=1280 broken=["Severity:Medium"]' and the same at 1440 px (the table is capped at 1168 px, so every desktop width is affected). Home mode breaks the times: 'fixed-06 ipv4 home 768 ... broken=["Last seen:01:31:42","Last seen:01:31:25","Last seen:01:38:21","Last seen:01:34:53"]'. The original (stages/ALL copy) at the same widths and data shows every pill on one line and broken=[] (e.g. 'orig-06 ipv6 analyst 1280 pills=High:1line,High:1line,Medium:1line,Medium:1line,Medium:1line sevCol=88px ... broken=[]'). Screenshots show the pills reading 'Mediu' / 'm' (shots/fixed-06-ipv4-analyst-768.png, shots/fixed-06-ipv6-analyst-1280.png). My rerun of the finding's s5e sweep reproduces its lines verbatim ('common analyst default shipped ... mid-word: 320:172.18.0.2:4437 701:unencrypted/Medium/Unencrypted 720:Medium 768:Medium 800:Medium 834:Medium 900:Medium 1024:Medium', stress '... 1024:unencrypted/Medium/Unencrypted 1280:Medium') and the V7 candidate has no mid-word break at any width, font or mode (its only sideways case, 701->720 with DejaVu Sans, also exists in the original: orig-06 home default at 701 already scrolls to 752). This is a real visual regression introduced by removing white-space: nowrap from .sev and putting overflow-wrap: anywhere on every .stack td.

Reran mutate.py against a fresh fixed-AHM-06 build (baseline: '57 passed in 4.16s'): exactly the 14 reversions listed survive, each printed as 'NOT CAUGHT (suite passes)' (lock-holder-no-stream, lock-no-relay, bfcache-no-abort, bfcache-no-rejoin, stream-502-no-retry, catchup-refresh-removed, again-flag-broken, filter-race-retarget-removed, upload-focus-removed, mode-switch-broken, not-saved-handler-dead, sev-nowrap-back, autocomplete-off-removed, actor-pattern-removed), while the 9 others are CAUGHT (hx-sync by its string check; text-field, both stale-form branches, QUEUE_LIMIT+1, timeline_end range, utc_time guard, home title, aside by real assertions). Not a test artifact: two of the surviving mutants were run in Chromium (scripts/f2_behaviour.js) with the suite green on them: 'lock-holder-no-stream    live refresh after upload: rows 1 -> 1 within 8030 ms (NO refresh in 8 s)' versus 'fixed-06 live refresh after upload: rows 1 -> 2 within 420 ms (refreshed)'; 'not-saved-handler-dead   Save with the server stopped -> message: null' versus the fixed build's 'No answer from the MaxGuard server: the change may not be saved. Reload the page to check.'. No file under tests/ other than tests/unit/test_web.py mentions app.js, autocomplete, pattern= or status-form, and there is no playwright/selenium suite anywhere in the repo. Caveat for severity: TestClient cannot exercise the JavaScript, so only the two template attributes (autocomplete="off", the actor pattern) are cheaply assertable; the rest needs a browser suite, and the original's test also only string-checked EventSource, so the gap is partly pre-existing. The factual claim stands.

Reran s6_caption.py on fixed-AHM-06 (250 alerts, 50 per severity, the least severe being the newest): GET / -> rows=200, first severities ['critical','critical','critical'], last ['low','low']; caption: 'The 200 most severe alerts, most recent first. More alerts match and are not shown: choose a status and a severity to see them.'; 'last seen of row 1 / row 2 / last row: 2026-10-06 15:20:50 UTC / 2026-10-06 15:20:49 UTC / 2026-10-06 15:22:31 UTC'; 'sorted most-recent-first? False; most-severe-first? True'. The query is 'ORDER BY severity_rank, last_seen DESC, finding_id' (state.py line 233, docstring 'Most severe first, then most recently seen'), and the unlimited caption on the same build reads '50 alerts, most severe first', so the two captions describe one ordering with contradicting words. The sentence is new in this change (the original caption is only '{{ alerts | length }} alerts, most severe first' and cut at 200 silently). Low severity, wording only, but a real inaccuracy of the fixed code.

Reproduced, but identically on the original: fixed-06 after the bad filter 'url: ?status=bogus&severity=, alertsDiv: false, rows: 0', gets '?status=&severity= -> 200 ; ?status=bogus&severity= -> 400', next stream event 'Cannot read properties of null (reading 'classList')', and choosing 'All' makes no request; orig-06 (stages/ALL copy): the same state and gets, error 'Cannot read properties of null (reading 'dispatchEvent')'. The table loss, the pushed URL and the dead filters are unchanged by this change; only the TypeError's wording differs. It is reachable only by editing an <option value> by hand: the server renders only valid option values, the refresh URL is built from validated values, and a hand-typed /?status=bogus is a full-page 400 with no table to lose (already covered by test_unknown_filter_value_is_a_400_page). An unchanged problem outside this change's scope; the suggested beforeSwap guard and the null check in refresh() are optional hardening.

Reproduced on fixed-AHM-06 (s7_hostile_form.py): case 4 '-> 200 'Saved.'; stored status='new' assignee='UploadFile(filename=\'x.txt\', size=7, headers=Headers({\'content-disposition\': \'form-data; name="assig'' (audited the same way); case 7 '-> 200 'Saved.'; stored ... assignee='Ann\x00Lee''. But the original build (stages/ALL copy) gives the byte-identical UploadFile repr for case 4 and also stores 'Ann\x00Lee' through its web form ('ORIGINAL web form, NUL assignee -> 200 stored: 'Ann\x00Lee''), and the JSON API does too ('PATCH /api/alerts -> 200 stored assignee: 'Ann\x00Lee''). Only a hostile multipart client can send a file part as 'assignee', and that client can already store any 100-character text by the ordinary route, so there is no impact beyond what the unchanged code and the API allow (no security issue, as the finding itself says). An unchanged problem outside the change's scope; the isinstance guard in text_field() is a cheap optional hardening.
